html:
Duke Kahanamoku was a Native Hawaiian swimmer and surfer from Waikīkī who won Olympic gold medals in swimming in 1912 and 1920. He is called the father of modern surfing.

Surfing, heʻe nalu, was an old Hawaiian practice that missionaries had frowned on. Duke and his friends at Waikīkī revived it, and he showed it off on visits to California and, in 1914 and 1915, to Australia, where it took hold.

He later served as sheriff of Honolulu and as a goodwill figure for Hawaii after statehood. Surfing became a world sport and an Olympic event in 2021, while staying tied to Polynesian identity. See also Kingdom of Hawaii.
